entries.title: Project overview and headline figures
entries.content: Dashboard Royale analyses The Gilded Ace, a fictional 300-machine casino, for January–June 2025 using synthetic data (data release 0.9.0-draft). Tracked casino net $15,585,460.60; tracked wagering $163,804,869.65; tracked payouts $148,219,409.05. Property coin-in $248,905,219.25, house win $23,638,155.10, theoretical win $23,545,364.48. 1,226 operations tickets (1,207 fault repairs), 5,021.08 downtime hours. Comp cost $190,669.30 (face value $682,749.50). 91 of 91 verification checks pass.

entries.title: Q1: Which machines are truly underperforming?
entries.content: Q1 separates luck, location and payout anomalies. The exposure-adjusted ranking compares each machine with same-configuration peers and gives 10 preliminary candidates: M-1014, M-1008, M-1045, M-1040, M-1230, M-1048, M-1265, M-1221, M-1227, M-1082, 10 of them in Back Forty. Re-ranked only against their own zone, 5 stay among the weakest (M-1008, M-1045, M-1230, M-1227, M-1082) and 5 are ordinary for their zone (M-1014, M-1040, M-1048, M-1265, M-1221), so their weakness is location. None has an unusual payout gap, so luck does not explain them. A payout test using each game's variance and spin count, corrected for testing 310 machines (|z| at least 3.77), flags: M-1158 held 3.04% vs an expected 10.00% (z = -4.62, below theo in 6 of 6 months). A flag is a reason to inspect, not proof of a fault.

entries.title: Q2: How did floor demand change?
entries.content: Q2 asks how floor demand changed across the months. Monthly floor coin-in changed unevenly from month to month rather than declining steadily: Jan $41.68M, Feb $39.58M, Mar $43.65M, Apr $41.29M, May $42.98M, Jun $39.73M. The highest month was Mar and the lowest Feb; January to June changed -4.7%. Change in daily coin-in per zone, January to June: Back Forty -10.1%; Bar Row -5.6%; Main Entrance -0.7%; Garage Entrance -5.9%; High-Limit Room -11.2%; Hotel Corridor -5.9%; Center Pit +10.5%. Daily foot traffic and coin-in are strongly correlated in Back Forty (r = 0.979), which is association, not proof that traffic causes play.

entries.title: Q2: Why demand moved — the W-ENT-B40 walkway closure
entries.content: The walkway between Main Entrance and Back Forty was closed for renovation from 2025-03-03 to 2025-04-06. Against the 35 days before, Back Forty coin-in per day changed -29.4% during the closure and -7.8% after it reopened; its foot traffic changed -30.4% during. Net of the rest of the floor (difference-in-differences) that is -32.9 points during and -6.7 after. Center Pit changed +8.7% during and +11.3% after, consistent with players re-routing. The windows are whole weeks with the same weekday mix; guest routes are not observed, so this is consistent with, not proof of, re-routing.

entries.title: Q3: How much play was lost to downtime?
entries.content: Q3 covers maintenance and downtime. There were 1,226 operations tickets, of which 1,207 were fault repairs; the others were installs, moves, scheduled maintenance and retirements. Total downtime was 5,021.08 hours (4,934.08 hours from fault repairs). An average fault repair waited 1.14 hours for a technician and took 2.95 hours to repair. Direct fault repair cost was $212,945.21. Estimated theoretical-win exposure from fault downtime was $88,346.72 — an upper-bound estimate, not actual lost revenue, because players can move to other machines. By manufacturer: Ridgeline 7.23 fault repairs per machine (680 repairs, 2,747 downtime hours, 94 machines); Northwind 3.02 fault repairs per machine (305 repairs, 1,288 downtime hours, 101 machines); Halcyon 1.93 fault repairs per machine (222 repairs, 899 downtime hours, 115 machines).

entries.title: Q4: What did tracked players wager, get back and net?
entries.content: Q4 covers tracked (loyalty-card) players, January–June. 113,890 players wagered $163,804,869.65 and were paid $148,219,409.05, a casino net of $15,585,460.60 (theoretical win $15,485,020.98). 80,992 players lost, 15,504 won and 17,394 broke even. Gross losses were $20,939,424.55 and winnings paid $5,353,963.95. Losses are concentrated: the top 1% of losing players account for 15.73% of gross losses, the top 5% for 40.73%, the top 10% for 52.84% and the top 20% for 66.52%. Gini coefficient of wagering 0.7536; of losses 0.6237.

entries.title: Q5: What did comps cost, and did anything change?
entries.content: Q5 covers the loyalty comp program. Actual economic comp cost was $190,669.30 against a face value of $682,749.50 (cost is 27.9% of face value), from 59,361 redemptions. From May 1 the points charged per comp dollar roughly halved in every tier (average points per face dollar, Jan–Apr to May–Jun: Base 15.0 to 7.0; Gold 12.0 to 5.6; Platinum 9.0 to 4.2). Average monthly comp cost rose from $30,812.60 (Jan–Apr) to $33,709.45 (May–Jun). Comp cost as a share of tracked theoretical win went from 1.11% in January to 1.32% in June. The data does not show whether the change was deliberate or whether it brought extra visits.

entries.title: Q6: Which actions would we fund with $100,000?
entries.content: Q6 asks which actions to fund with $100,000 for the 30 days from July 1, 2025. Up to 3 action types are allowed; keeping money (A-HOLD) does not use a slot. The plan: A-INSPECT (Machine inspection and paytable verification) quantity 5 at $1,200 each = $6,000, lead time 1 days, 29 days of effect; A-WAYFINDING (Wayfinding and signage refresh for a zone) quantity 1 at $7,500 each = $7,500, lead time 10 days, 20 days of effect; A-COMP-PILOT (Comp policy pilot with control group) quantity 1 at $4,000 each = $4,000, lead time 5 days, 25 days of effect. Total invested $17,500; preserved $82,500.

entries.title: Q6: Why these actions were chosen
entries.content: Each action answers one cause found in the data. A-INSPECT checks M-1158, M-1054, M-1210, M-1010, M-1201: the lowest payout z-scores on the floor; scenarios low net $-6,165; base net $-371; high net $10,367; break-even 37% of their combined shortfall. A-WAYFINDING adds signs for the zone behind the closed walkway, which stayed 6.7 points below the rest of the floor after reopening; scenarios low net $-7,500; base net $2,363; high net $12,226; break-even 38% recovery of that gap. A-COMP-PILOT tests the May 1 comp pricing change with a randomised control group; scenarios low net $-4,000; base net $-3,396; high net $-2,793; it does not pay back within 30 days and is funded for the pricing decision, worth up to $34,762 a year. An extra technician is not funded: removing all waiting time would recover at most $4,089 per 30 days.

entries.title: Q6: How we would know the actions worked
entries.content: Inspections: paytable and meter checks per machine, then July hold versus configured hold, run on the quietest forecast days (2025-07-08, 2025-07-15, 2025-07-22, 2025-07-29, 2025-07-02). Signage: the zone's entries per counter-hour and coin-in versus its pre-closure level, net of the other zones; measured at zone level because the best-case effect (0.75% of floor coin-in) is below what the forecast can detect at floor level (about 1.1%). Comp pilot: comp cost per dollar of theo and trips per player, treatment versus randomised control.

entries.title: Q6: Actions considered but not funded
entries.content: Considered but not funded: A-TECH-SHIFT (Add one technician to a shift for 30 days, $11,520); A-PREVENTIVE (Preventive maintenance sweep for one manufacturer, $9,000); A-REPLACE-LEASE (Replace a machine with a leased new title, $33,800); A-REPLACE-BUY (Replace a machine with a purchased new title, $220,000); A-COMP-CHANGE (Change comp redemption rate floor-wide, $1,500); A-PROMO (Property promotion weekend, $15,000). The technician cannot recover its cost; preventive maintenance is a candidate for the next horizon; replacements would put new titles in the same low-traffic spot; a promotion's benefit is not established causally; a floor-wide comp change is mutually exclusive with the pilot.

entries.title: Forecast model of daily coin-in
entries.content: A daily coin-in forecast was trained on 2025-01-01 to 2025-04-30 and tested on 2025-05-01 to 2025-06-30. Holdout error: Baseline 1 — training mean: MAE $218,258; Baseline 2 — weekday average: MAE $68,699; Weekday avg + AR(1) residual: MAE $68,624; Calendar regression (weekday + holiday + known events + trend): MAE $65,187. The calendar regression improves on the weekday average by $3,511 MAE, but the 95% confidence interval ($-4,530 to $16,591) includes zero, so the gain is not statistically conclusive. It picks the same July quiet days as the weekday baseline; its main use is the error estimate, which decides that Q6 effects are measured at zone or machine level rather than against total floor coin-in.

entries.title: Claim: Of the 10 config-ranked candidates, 5 are weak even within their own zone; 5 only look weak because of where they stand.
entries.content: Claim: Of the 10 config-ranked candidates, 5 are weak even within their own zone; 5 only look weak because of where they stand. Result: M-1014 rank 14/47; M-1008 rank 3/47; M-1045 rank 6/47; M-1040 rank 19/47; M-1230 rank 4/47; M-1048 rank 25/47; M-1265 rank 13/47; M-1221 rank 23/47; M-1227 rank 7/47; M-1082 rank 8/47. Calculation: zone_score = 0.6(1 - pct_zone(theo/hr / config median)) + 0.4(1 - pct_zone(occupancy)); machine-specific if in the weakest 20% of its zone. Alternative explanation considered: All ten are simply in a quiet zone (location) (tested: Re-ranked every machine against its own zone; half stay near the bottom). Limitation: The 20% cut-off and 0.6/0.4 weights are judgement calls; dominant zone used for machines that moved.

entries.title: Claim: The candidates' low results are not bad luck.
entries.content: Claim: The candidates' low results are not bad luck. Result: Payout z-scores of the 10 candidates range -0.06 to +2.23; none below -2.58. Calculation: z = (house_win/coin_in - theo/coin_in) / sqrt(payout_multiplier_variance x bet_mix_factor / paid_spins). Alternative explanation considered: High-volatility variance hid a weak machine (tested: Variance-scaled z-score per machine using the game's own payout variance). Limitation: Bet sizes per spin are not in the data; an equal mix of the listed bets is assumed (more conservative than equal bets).

entries.title: Claim: M-1158 paid out significantly more than its configuration allows: a lead to inspect, not proof of a fault.
entries.content: Claim: M-1158 paid out significantly more than its configuration allows: a lead to inspect, not proof of a fault. Result: Hold 3.04% vs expected 10.00%; z = -4.62 (flag 3.77 after correcting for 310 machines); below theo in 6 of 6 months; 1 machine(s) flagged in total. Calculation: Bonferroni two-sided 5% threshold across 310 machines; months below theo vs Binomial(n, 0.5). Alternative explanation considered: An unlucky streak on a medium-volatility game (tested: Shortfall exceeds the multiple-testing threshold and persists across months). Limitation: Statistical evidence only; an inspection must confirm. No wrongdoing is implied.

entries.title: Claim: The W-ENT-B40 walkway closure (2025-03-03 to 2025-04-06) coincides with Back Forty's steepest drop, and the zone has not fully recovered since it reopened.
entries.content: Claim: The W-ENT-B40 walkway closure (2025-03-03 to 2025-04-06) coincides with Back Forty's steepest drop, and the zone has not fully recovered since it reopened. Result: Coin-in/day -29.4% during and -7.8% after vs the 35 days before; net of the rest of the floor -32.9 pp during, -6.7 pp after; entries/hr -30.4% during. Calculation: Equal 5-week windows (same weekday mix); difference-in-differences = zone % change - rest-of-floor % change. Alternative explanation considered: Citywide seasonality or events (March tournament, CinemaCon, NAB) (tested: Difference-in-differences nets out swings that hit every zone). Limitation: Closure timing is the only change tested; traffic counts are entries, not visitors.

entries.title: Claim: Center Pit gained while the walkway was closed, and kept the gain after it reopened.
entries.content: Claim: Center Pit gained while the walkway was closed, and kept the gain after it reopened. Result: Center Pit coin-in/day +8.7% during, +11.3% after (net of the rest of the floor +12.1 / +18.0 pp). Calculation: Same windows and difference-in-differences as above. Alternative explanation considered: Center Pit was already growing before the closure (tested: Monthly trend shown on the page; gain concentrated from March). Limitation: Consistent with displaced players, but individual routes are not observed.

entries.title: Claim: Downtime and lost play are measured consistently from two independent sources.
entries.content: Claim: Downtime and lost play are measured consistently from two independent sources. Result: 5,021.08 h downtime (1,226 tickets, 1,207 fault repairs); estimated fault exposure $88,346.72. Calculation: downtime = available_at - opened_at (UTC); exposure = fault downtime x machine theo per available hour. Alternative explanation considered: Players switch to a nearby machine (tested: Exposure labelled an upper bound). Limitation: Average play rate assumed; not actual lost revenue.

entries.title: Claim: Ridgeline machines are the main source of repairs.
entries.content: Claim: Ridgeline machines are the main source of repairs. Result: Ridgeline 7.23, Northwind 3.02, Halcyon 1.93 tickets per machine. Calculation: tickets / machines per manufacturer. Alternative explanation considered: Ridgeline machines are older or busier (tested: Normalised by fleet size). Limitation: Age and usage not controlled.

entries.title: Claim: Tracked players' net result and its concentration.
entries.content: Claim: Tracked players' net result and its concentration. Result: Wagered $163,804,869.65, paid $148,219,409.05, casino net $15,585,460.60; top 5% of losers = 40.73% of gross losses; wagering Gini 0.7536. Calculation: casino net = sum coin-in - sum payout; Gini over per-player totals. Alternative explanation considered: A few lucky or unlucky sessions (tested: Results shown for every month range). Limitation: Carded play only; within-period netting.

entries.title: Claim: Points charged per comp dollar halved on May 1 in every tier.
entries.content: Claim: Points charged per comp dollar halved on May 1 in every tier. Result: Base 15.0 -> 7.0; Gold 12.0 -> 5.6; Platinum 9.0 -> 4.2; comp cost $190,669.30 reconciles across three sources. Calculation: points per $ = -sum(points_delta) / (sum(face_value_cents) / 100) over redemptions. Alternative explanation considered: Tier mix shift (tested: Every tier halved on the same day). Limitation: No policy record; cause not attributed.

entries.title: Claim: The calendar model forecasts slightly better than a weekday average, but does not change the July schedule.
entries.content: Claim: The calendar model forecasts slightly better than a weekday average, but does not change the July schedule. Result: Holdout MAE $65,187 vs weekday $68,699 vs mean $218,258; gain 95% CI -$4,530 to $16,591; same quiet days as the baseline: True. Calculation: Train Jan 1-Apr 30, frozen; holdout May 1-Jun 30; 7-day moving-block bootstrap of the MAE gain. Alternative explanation considered: Holdout noise (tested: Bootstrap interval; two baselines). Limitation: Four months of training.

entries.title: Claim: The forecast decides how each action is measured: floor-level effects of these actions would be invisible.
entries.content: Claim: The forecast decides how each action is measured: floor-level effects of these actions would be invisible. Result: Detection limit over 20 days ~1.07% of floor coin-in; best-case signage effect 0.75% -> measure at zone level against other zones. Calculation: detection limit = MAE / sqrt(days) / mean daily coin-in. Alternative explanation considered: Measure everything against total floor coin-in (tested: Compared each effect with the forecast's error). Limitation: Treats daily errors as independent.

entries.title: Claim: Inspecting 5 machines breaks even if 37% of their combined shortfall is real.
entries.content: Claim: Inspecting 5 machines breaks even if 37% of their combined shortfall is real. Result: low: net -$6,165; base: net -$371; high: net $10,367. Calculation: benefit = sum(daily shortfall) x operating days; cost includes inspection downtime at each machine's theo/hr. Alternative explanation considered: The shortfalls are luck (tested: Low scenario assumes exactly that). Limitation: Correction assumed to restore configured hold at once.

entries.title: Claim: Signage for Back Forty breaks even at 38% recovery of the gap left after the walkway reopened.
entries.content: Claim: Signage for Back Forty breaks even at 38% recovery of the gap left after the walkway reopened. Result: Remaining gap $986 theo/day; low: net -$7,500; base: net $2,363; high: net $12,226. Calculation: gap = -DiD(after) x pre-closure theo/day; benefit = gap x recovery x operating days. Alternative explanation considered: The zone would recover anyway (tested: Measured against other zones over the same days). Limitation: Signage effect size unknown; theo, not profit.

entries.title: Claim: The comp pilot does not pay back within 30 days; it is funded for the decision it informs.
entries.content: Claim: The comp pilot does not pay back within 30 days; it is funded for the decision it informs. Result: In-horizon savings at most $1,207 vs $4,000; the pricing decision is worth up to $34,762/year. Calculation: savings = (May-Jun - Jan-Apr monthly comp cost) x treatment share x days/30. Alternative explanation considered: Change comp rates floor-wide instead (tested: A floor-wide change cannot separate pricing from seasonality). Limitation: 25 days may be too short to see visit changes.

entries.title: Claim: An extra technician is not funded: it cannot recover its cost.
entries.content: Claim: An extra technician is not funded: it cannot recover its cost. Result: Waiting time is 27.9% of fault downtime -> at most $4,089 per 30 days vs $11,520. Calculation: max recovery = fault exposure per 30 days x response share. Alternative explanation considered: Faster response also shortens repairs (tested: Upper bound assumes all waiting is removed). Limitation: Ignores coverage benefits.
